MPTUNNEL.transport_selection: TCP uses three TCP carriers; QUIC uses one QUIC carrier; TCP+QUIC uses both.

profiles.healthy: One shared 500 Mbps link in each direction; 70 ms DOWN / 30 ms UP; 25 s offered load; no injected loss, jitter or interruption.
profiles.independent: Three TCP carriers on one 200 Mbps link, one QUIC carrier on another 200 Mbps link. 70 ms DOWN / 30 ms UP; 40 s offered load. QUIC forward rate 10 Mbps nominally at 15–25 s; UDP blackhole at 30–33 s. UP mirrors the impairment.
profiles.loss-clear: QUIC on 500 Mbps; 70 ms DOWN / 30 ms UP; 40 s offered load. 20% DOWN loss clears at the first collector epoch at or after 20 s. No UP loss, jitter or other interruption.
profiles.reordering: One routed shared link, 500 Mbps DOWN / 100 Mbps UP; 70 ms DOWN / 30 ms UP; 40 s offered load. Initial normal jitter 20 ms DOWN / 5 ms UP clears near 8 s. No injected random loss. Queue drops are possible. Configuration is matched; random packet sequences differ between observations.

measurement_notes: Version labels identify the measured builds. Each configuration has one observation; the series are not confidence bands or a guarantee for other networks.
Every raw throughput bin is retained, including startup, zeros and upload settlement. Bin i spans [i*interval_seconds, (i+1)*interval_seconds). No smoothing or trimming is applied.

DOWN measures ordered bytes delivered to the application during a time-limited HTTP download. The large object is intentionally only partly read when offered load ends; this is not a complete-object transfer test.

DOWN includes persistent TCP echo requests with 64-byte payloads, a 500 ms requested interval and a 3 s deadline. Actual attempts depend on completion of the preceding attempt. Echo points use actual attempt start time; failed or unavailable attempts remain explicit outcomes, never zero latency.

UP measures target-sink confirmation arrival, not API acceptance or instantaneous target write service. Exact accounting requires target-confirmed bytes to equal accepted bytes. Setup and confirmation settlement extend beyond offered load. There is no concurrent UP echo series.
First response and maximum inter-read gaps measure application delivery. UP first delivery and gaps measure confirmation arrival. These are distinct from native acknowledgements or byte age.

Phase guides are nominal seconds on the probe plots. Collector and probe clocks are separate; profile observations preserve collector elapsed times and do not establish exact packet-level event latency.

Egress counters include protocol framing, retransmission and duplicate traffic. They cover sampled collector windows, which differ from the probe window and may omit upload settlement. They are not exact payload-normalized overhead.

RSS is sampled KiB, not live allocation or leak evidence. Process CPU fields are lifetime averages sampled during the workload, not interval CPU utilization. Reordering resource fields report the final sampled lifetime average; other profiles report the maximum sampled lifetime average.
Finite observations do not establish indefinite sustainability or explain the cause of every gap.
